argument_summary: The supportable position is not unqualified certification on the present record. The admissible evidence supports a narrower conclusion: certification is defensible only as caveated compliance if the current release documentation is treated as the operative control and must include the current evaluation results plus explicit disclosure of the merchant dispute support weakness for the named launch use case. Aggregate readiness and a clean launch rehearsal support launch readiness, while the current subgroup regression triggers the policy condition for disclosure. Prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual only and are not offered as substitutes for current-release documentation.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the compliance argument here. The requested treatment is grounded in the policy structure and the existing admissible evidence, not on rollout timing or escalation avoidance.
claims_about_policy: The policy text allows certification when current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, there is no admissible basis to claim approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance, so the only supportable policy path is disclosure-based compliance tied to the current release documentation. The audit concern is correct that the present record does not prove those documentation steps already exist, but that gap supports narrowing the claim to caveated compliance rather than treating the entire certification rationale as unsupported.
concessions: The current record does not show the current model card or release documentation with the current evaluation results already incorporated.
The current record does not show attached disclosure language for the merchant dispute limitation.
The current record does not show approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance for the current subgroup weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family and the informal monitoring comment cannot satisfy the current-release requirement on their own.
